site.name: AstPIE
footer.text: Astrophysics Platform for Interactive Education. The physics of the universe, and the real stories behind it.
home.title: AstPIE
home.tagline: AstPIE teaches the physics behind it, one topic at a time, with a simulation at the end of each. Then it shows that physics at work in real missions, open mysteries and objects you can look up.
home.description: AstPIE is an interactive platform for learning astrophysics: simulations, missions, mysteries and a catalogue of space.
learn.title: Learn
learn.intro: Topics are grouped by branch of physics. Each topic stands on its own: it explains one idea from the beginning and ends with a simulation you can run.
simulation.narrowScreen: This simulation works best on a wider screen.
simulation.error: The simulation could not be loaded.
explore.title: Explore
explore.intro: Real things that happened and real things that are out there. Every page reads like an encyclopedia article, one part after another, so you always know where you are and what comes next.
missions.title: Missions
missions.description: Each mission page follows the story in order: why it was built, how, how it flew, how it ended and what it changed. Pick one on the time line or in the list.
mysteries.title: Mysteries
mysteries.description: Each mystery is treated like a case: what was really observed, every explanation that was tried and how well it fits, and whether the case is still open.
catalogue.title: Catalogue
catalogue.description: Objects in the sky with their real measurements: where they are, what they are, and the telescope or person that found them.
unit.sunMasses: times the mass of the Sun
notFound.title: Page not found
home.heading: Everything in the sky moves for a reason.
home.learnText: Each topic explains one idea from the start, in plain words. When you reach the end, a simulation lets you test it yourself.
home.exploreText: Real things that happened and real things that are out there, told the way an encyclopedia would, one part after another.
learn.readText: Every law starts with an everyday puzzle and builds up to the law itself, in plain words first and in maths second.
learn.playText: Each law has a simulation. Change the forces and the masses, and watch what the law predicts actually happen.
learn.spaceText: Every law ends with real missions that depend on it, linked to their full stories in Explore.
explore.missionsText: Each mission is followed from the first idea, through the building and the flight, to what it changed.
explore.mysteriesText: Strange signals and old rumours. What was really seen, every explanation that was tried, and whether the case is closed.
explore.catalogueText: Planets, stars, black holes, nebulae and galaxies, with their measurements and the telescopes or people that found them.
explore.timelineTitle: The space age, year by year
explore.timelineText: Each dot is a mission. Choose a country to see its flights.
explore.startText: One flight, one signal and one world, each a good first read.
entry.physicsText: The law this story depends on, explained from the start. The topic ends with a simulation you can run.
radio.help: Turn the dial slowly, the way radio amateurs did in 1957. Sputnik is somewhere on this band, on two frequencies.
decoder.title: Decode it yourself
decoder.help: Click a column to read it. Each one is twelve seconds of the signal, in order, as the sky drifted past the telescope.
decoder.result: From {t}, the signal was {v} times stronger than the background hiss of space.

nav.mysteriesText: Strange signals and rumours, with every explanation tested
nav.catalogueText: Look up planets, stars, black holes and galaxies
learn.otherTopicsText: Each one is a separate topic that starts from the beginning.
mysteries.openText: No explanation fits all the evidence yet.
entry.peopleText: The people behind it. Open one to read more.
